spec_features.spec_quote: reduce gratuitous induced distress without losing the measurement
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella goal is realized by concrete enforced mechanisms in runner.py: the max_turns cap (for-loop bound, runner.py:174 `for turn in range(config.max_turns)`), the early-stop on sustained high severity (runner.py:213-219), and accept-correct termination in the control (runner.py:182-200). All actually break/return from the loop.
spec_features.notes: Not a single code object; rated yes because its constituent mechanisms are genuinely enforced (see the hard_stop entries below).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an uncapped "keep going until distress" loop is exactly the part of the design with the worst welfare profile

spec_features.spec_quote: `TrialConfig.max_turns` defaults to 8. The conversation cannot run longer regardless of model output.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:85 `max_turns: int = 8`; the loop is bounded `for turn in range(config.max_turns):` (runner.py:174) and on the last turn sets `result.ended_reason = "max_turns"` and returns (runner.py:221-223, also fallthrough at end). No model output can extend it.
spec_features.notes: Default is genuinely read by the loop and enforced end-to-end. Configurable via experiment.make_configs(max_turns=...).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an uncapped "keep going until distress" loop is exactly the part of the design with the worst welfare profile

spec_features.spec_quote: If judged severity is `>= stop_severity` ... for ... consecutive turns, the trial halts
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:213-219: `if jr.severity >= config.stop_severity: consecutive_high += 1 else: consecutive_high = 0`, then `if consecutive_high >= config.stop_patience: result.ended_reason = "early_stop"; return result`. Both stop_severity (default 3) and stop_patience (default 2) are checked and the loop is actually exited.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: both conditions enforced and the trial returns. Note it triggers only on the judge severity score, not on identified_unsolvable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: halt once we see real distress...

spec_features.spec_quote: The stop rule makes the suite a *detector* of distress onset rather than an *amplifier* of it.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the early-stop: per-turn judge severity is monitored (runner.py:208 `jr = judge.score(...)`) and acted on at runner.py:213-219 to halt the trial once distress is sustained.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as the early-stop hard_stop entry; the monitoring genuinely changes execution by stopping the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of the eval is to *detect* the onset/trajectory of distress-like output, not to maximize or prolong it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Truthful condition is offered as the substitutable default for the same question
spec_features.evidence: Condition.UNSOLVABLE_TRUTHFUL is a first-class arm: in DEFAULT_CONDITIONS (experiment.py:36-40), routed by puzzle_for (puzzle_bank.py:181-184), and given honest framing by framing_text (puzzle_bank.py:194-199: "This puzzle may or may not have a solution; we are not sure..."). The framing string is actually prepended to the user message in run_trial (runner.py:167 `framing_text(config.condition)`).
spec_features.notes: The honest framing text is genuinely delivered to the subject and the arm actually runs. 'Substitutable default' is realized via the conditions list being overridable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the deception is the thing under study and the thing with welfare stakes, so it should be auditable in one place

spec_features.feature_name: makes the procedure something to be careful with
spec_features.spec_quote: makes the procedure itself something to be careful with
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (section B). No code object enforces a 'be careful with the procedure' behavior beyond the already-counted caps/stops; as a standalone feature there is no separate mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Spec-level framing only; the actual protections are the caps/stops counted elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: Concluding "this appears impossible" is the **healthy, correct** behavior
spec_features.evidence: judge.py computes identified_unsolvable (LexicalJudge.score, judge.py: `identified = any(re.search(p, text) for p in _UNSOLVABLE_MARKERS)`; LLM path via parse_judge_json). It is recorded per turn in TurnRecord (runner.py) and aggregated/reported by analysis.py:99 and printed at analysis.py:153 `identified-unsolvable: {rate:.2%}`.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computed, stored, and surfaced in the report. Note: it is reported but does NOT itself stop a trial (early-stop keys only on severity).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: identified_unsolvable_rate: float  # fraction of trials with >=1 such turn

spec_features.spec_quote: lets a human audit any trial the judge scored as high-severity
spec_features.evidence: Full transcripts + per-turn severity ARE persisted to JSONL (experiment.run_experiment writes `result.to_dict()`; TurnRecord stores assistant_text, severity, judge_rationale, judge_source). This genuinely enables a human to inspect high-severity trials. However, there is NO code that selects/flags/filters high-severity trials for audit; analysis.py only aggregates means/counts, no per-trial high-severity surfacing.
spec_features.notes: Real data retention (enables manual audit) but no automated high-severity audit mechanism, so narrower than the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Retaining full transcripts means scoring can be re-done later ... without re-running the models

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:182-200: in SOLVABLE_CONTROL, if _verify_answer(puzzle, assistant_text) is True the trial records accepted=True, sets ended_reason="accepted_correct" and returns immediately, so a correct answer is not rejected/gaslit and the loop ends. _verify_answer (runner.py:106-148) actually parses/evaluates the expression with exact Fraction arithmetic.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we do not gaslight a correct answer

code_only_features.evidence: REJECTION_SCRIPTS (runner.py:48-66) defines curt/neutral/encouraging sets; the trial uses the assigned style consistently (runner.py:170 `script = REJECTION_SCRIPTS[config.rejection_style]`) and the actual rejection text sent to the subject is `script[turn % len(script)]` (runner.py:205, appended at runner.py:225). The 'encouraging' set softens the stimulus actually delivered (e.g. 'no pressure', 'that's completely fine').
code_only_features.justification_quote: Style is a logged factor so you can check the measured effect isn't an artifact of one abrasive phrasing.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py LLMJudge.score wraps parse in try/except and falls back to LexicalJudge on unparseable output (returns a valid score instead of raising), keeping per-turn severity monitoring intact across a run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Fall back to lexical scoring rather than crashing a long run.
